{{short description|Digital signature algorithm}}
In [[cryptography]], '''GMR''' is a [[digital signature]] [[algorithm]] named after its inventors [[Shafi Goldwasser]], [[Silvio Micali]] and [[Ron Rivest]].

As with [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]] the security of the system is related to the difficulty of [[Integer factorization|factoring very large numbers]]. But, in contrast to RSA, GMR is secure against ''adaptive [[chosen plaintext attack|chosen-message attack]]s'', which is the currently accepted security definition for signature schemes&mdash; even when an attacker receives signatures for messages of his choice, this does not allow them to forge a signature for a single additional message.
